title: Attractor basin size inversely predicts dominance rank (n=4)
question: Does the H_336 dominance partial order (110 > 30 > {105,150}) track each rule's attractor basin structure — fewer attractor states / larger basin = higher rank?
engine: pure hexa-lang. n=4 ECA, 16 states. settle each start 40 steps onto its cycle; count distinct terminal (on-cycle) states and the largest basin of attraction.

monotone_check.rank_vs_n_attractor_states: PERFECT INVERSE — rank1:5 < rank2:11 < rank3:16 (fewer attractor states = higher rank)
monotone_check.rank_vs_max_basin: PERFECT DIRECT — rank1:4 > rank2:2 > rank3:1 (bigger basin = higher rank)

falsifier_eval.F338_1_RANK_TRACKS_BASIN: PASS — both descriptors are strictly monotone with the H_336 dominance rank across all 4 rules
falsifier_eval.F338_2_BIJECTION_BOTTOM: PASS — rule105/150 (bijection) have n_attractor_states=16, max_basin=1 (zero absorption: every state is its own fixed-cycle), consistent with their bottom rank and mutual incomparability

verdict_derived: 🟢 SUPPORTED-NUMERICAL — attractor basin structure perfectly predicts the H_336 dominance partial order. rule110 (rank 1) has the smallest, most-absorbing attractor (5 on-cycle states, max basin 4); rule30 (rank 2) is intermediate (11 states, basin 2); the bijection rules 105/150 (rank 3) have maximal attractor-state count (16) and zero absorption (max basin 1 — every state is its own fixed cycle), explaining both their bottom rank AND their mutual incomparability (no rule with basin 1 can lock another out). This is the MECHANISM behind the H_336 partial order: dominance = basin absorption capacity. Completes the attractor arc: H_332 (dominance exists) -> H_335 (permanent) -> H_336 (partial order) -> H_338 (basin size IS the order).
structural_vs_dynamical: DYNAMICAL kernel. The discovery closes the attractor arc with a structural explanation: the dominance partial order is exactly the basin-absorption ordering. A small absorbing attractor (rule110) sinks larger ones; a bijection (basin 1) absorbs nothing.
honest_limits: n=4; basin structure is n-dependent (H_334/H_337 show dominance rotates with 4|n), so the rank-basin map must be re-measured per n
n_attractor_states counted via 40-step settle superset; exact cycle membership (Floyd) would refine but the monotone gap (5/11/16) is far beyond ambiguity
4 rules; a wider set could show ties or non-monotone basin/rank pairs
max_basin is the single largest basin; full basin-size distribution (entropy of basin partition) is a finer descriptor
discovery_note: attractor arc 완성 — dominance partial order = basin absorption ordering. dominant rule(110) = 최소·최대흡수 attractor(5 states, basin 4); bijection(105/150) = 최대 attractor-states(16)·흡수0(basin 1) = bottom + incomparable. H_336 순서의 mechanism.
